records.text: Nicolae and Elena Ceaușescu were executed on Christmas Day 1989 after a show trial.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Christmas Day of 1989, the then president, Nicolae Ceaușescu, and his wife, Elena Ceaușescu, were actually ruthlessly murdered after a show trial.

verification.notes: Romania's official communiqué records the extraordinary military tribunal, death sentence, and execution of Nicolae and Elena Ceausescu on December 25, 1989; independent historical material characterizes the summary proceeding as a show or kangaroo trial.

records.text: A Romanian viewer says General Gica Popa died by suicide three months after sentencing Nicolae Ceausescu and his wife to death, leaving a note that he could not live with the guilt.
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #1 (Ep DdPjoy5W-wY)

appearances.snippet: The cruelty of that killing has haunted our country for years. General Gica Popa committed suicide right after being forced to sentence them to death by firing squad. ... committed suicide right after being forced to sentence them to death by firing squad. Three months after the execution, he shot himself in the head in his office at the Ministry of National Defense, leaving a note stating that he couldn't live with the guilt anymore.

verification.notes: Gica Popa did die by suicide after his trial and conviction, but contemporaneous reporting places the death a little over two months—not three months—after the trial and says his note asked forgiveness without explaining his motive. The claim’s timing is approximate and its assertion that guilt caused the suicide is unsupported.

sources.title: Los Angeles Times: Romanian General Convicted in Massacre Kills Himself
sources.relevance: Contemporaneous report confirms Gica Popa’s suicide after conviction and describes his note, which asked forgiveness but did not say guilt drove the suicide.
